summary: SLA priority hysteresis causing repeated misrouting to Tier-2 queue
description:
Issue summary:
Support routing is repeatedly sending P1 customer tickets to the Tier-2 escalation queue after SLA window extensions. The problem appears related to priority hysteresis logic in the SLA engine: when SLA windows extend (e.g., extended first_response_due_at), downstream routing incorrectly re-evaluates priority and applies an upward escalation that should be idempotent.

Impact:
- Approximately 8-12% of P1 tickets created in the last 36 hours were re-routed to Tier-2 after a delayed SLA refresh.
- Increased load on Tier-2 on-call and delayed resolution for priority lanes that expect a single escalation hop.
- Observed duplicate notifications to on-call Slack channel (#oncall-tier2) and PagerDuty triggers in some cases.

Environment:
- Production (prod) in us-east-1 only observed so far.
- Affects support-tooling stack: SLA engine service (v2.4.1), routing-evaluator (v1.9.0), and the enrichment pipeline that applies macros/templates.

Steps to reproduce (observed flow):
1) Create a P1 customer ticket with customer_tier=dedicated and no initial assignment (SUP intake).
2) SLA engine computes initial priority and sets first_response_due_at.
3) Automated enrichment updates ticket metadata (adds escalation_hint) after 15m due to missing agent assignment.
4) SLA refresh job runs (periodic refresh triggered by kafka topic sla-refresh) and extends the SLA window because enrichment changed fields.
5) Routing-evaluator receives updated priority and applies escalation policy, routing ticket to Tier-2 even though the ticket already had a previous escalation record.

Observed logs / telemetry snippets:
- sla-engine logs: "refresh_sla: ticket=INT-76241 prev_priority=P1 new_priority=P1 reason=window-extended" (2026-03-05T14:22:03Z)
- routing-evaluator logs: "apply_escalation: ticket=INT-76241 target_queue=tier-2 force=true source=sla-refresh" (2026-03-05T14:22:04Z)
- enrichment pipeline: "macro_attach: ticket=INT-76241 added=escalation_hint=high_reassign" (2026-03-05T14:21:59Z)
- telemetry snapshot: reroute_count by hour shows spikes correlating with sla-refresh cron at hh:22.

Initial hypothesis:
- The SLA refresh path marks priority as changed when only the due timestamp changed. Downstream routing checks both priority and "changed_at" timestamp and treats any change as a candidate for forced escalation. There is missing idempotency guard for escalations tied only to timestamp shifts.

Impact analysis and risk:
- Medium-high operational risk: frequent noisy escalations could mask real Tier-2 incidents and increase MTTR.
- Low risk for data loss. Changes to evaluator logic must be safe-guarded with feature flag.

Proposed immediate mitigation:
- Add a temporary rule in routing-evaluator to ignore escalations where prev_priority == new_priority and the only delta is first_response_due_at within a tolerance window (e.g., 5 minutes). Deploy as a runtime config flag.
- Throttle automatic re-route actions to limit duplicate route events to 1 per ticket per 1h until permanent fix is deployed.

Permanent fix suggestions:
- Update SLA engine to emit a delta payload that explicitly lists what changed (priority, due_timestamp, severity) so routing can make deterministic decisions.
- Add idempotency token on escalation events persisted in routing DB to prevent duplicate actions.
- Add unit/integration tests for edge cases where only SLA timestamps change.

Required follow-ups:
- Run backfill to identify tickets impacted in last 48 hours and add manual rollback where Tier-2 assignment is incorrect.
- Postmortem draft if customer-impacting trends exceed threshold (10% of P1s misrouted).
steps_to_reproduce: Create P1 ticket with no assignment and dedicated tier
Trigger enrichment macro that adds escalation_hint after 10-20m
Wait for sla-refresh cron job to run and observe routing-evaluator behavior
investigation_notes: Checked sla-refresh consumer offsets in Kafka: no lag observed; messages processed in sequence.
Replayed update for a test ticket in staging and reproduced reroute when only due_timestamp changed.
Event payload from sla-engine lacks a structured 'changed_fields' array; it only emits ticket diff as freeform text.
comments: Emily Chen (Reporter) [2026-03-05]: Initial report filed after noticing multiple Tier-2 notifications during the 14:00 window. Added logs and telemetry charts.
Priya Nair (SRE) [2026-03-05]: I see the same pattern in PagerDuty alerts. Temporarily muting reroute notifications on #oncall-tier2 to reduce noise; will not resolve routing actions.
Raj Patel (Assignee) [2026-03-06]: Starting root-cause triage. Reproduced in staging. Creating feature-flagged patch to routing-evaluator to ignore timestamp-only diffs.
Ana Gomez (Platform Eng) [2026-03-08]: Submitted PR to routing-evaluator to add idempotency key storage: https://github.com/redwood-inference/route-evaluator/pull/289. Needs QA and canary.
CS Lead - Marcus Lee [2026-03-09]: Please prepare a customer-impact brief if we see escalation rates continue; notify accounts with potential delays.
resolution_notes: In progress: feature-flagged guard merged to routing-evaluator canary and rolled out to 10% of pods on 2026-03-09. Early telemetry shows 90% reduction in duplicate escalations for canary traffic. Next steps: full rollout after 48h canary and SLA-engine signature change to include structured changed_fields. Manual fixes for 17 affected tickets in the last 24h are in the backlog assigned to CS ops.
workaround: Enable routing-evaluator runtime config 'ignore_timestamp_only_sla_changes=true' and set reroute_throttle_per_ticket=1h. Manual reassignment for misrouted tickets via support console.
resolution_status: Partial mitigation applied; permanent fix planned (SLA engine contract change + idempotency).
notes_for_postmortem: Quantify total P1 misroutes in 72h window
Timeline of changes to sla-refresh consumer and enrichment macro rollout
Evaluate adding schema to SLA events (changed_fields) and updating routing contract
